raw_record.question_text: Hanni wants to colour in the circles in the diagram. When two circles are connected by a line they should have different colours. What is the minimum number of colours she needs?

method.method_draft: First translate the picture into a graph: label the seven circles as left-middle, upper-left, lower-left, centre, upper-right, right-middle, and lower-right. From the image, note especially that the lower-left circle, centre circle, and lower-right circle are all pairwise connected: lower-left--centre, centre--lower-right, and lower-left--lower-right. Because three mutually connected circles form a triangle, they require three different colours, so at least 3 colours are necessary. Then show 3 colours are enough by assigning three different colours to that triangle and checking the remaining four circles can be coloured consistently, e.g. upper-left can share the lower-right colour, left-middle can share the centre colour, upper-right can share the lower-left colour, and right-middle can share the centre colour. Therefore the minimum is 3.

method.method_draft: Try to decide whether 2 colours could work. From the image, follow the closed cycle lower-left -> centre -> lower-right -> lower-left. These three connecting lines make an odd cycle of length 3. If only two colours were available, lower-left and centre would need opposite colours, centre and lower-right would need opposite colours, forcing lower-left and lower-right to have the same colour; but the image shows lower-left and lower-right are directly connected, so this is impossible. Thus at least 3 colours are needed. To verify that 3 suffice, colour the lower-left, centre, and lower-right circles with three different colours, then fill the upper-left, left-middle, upper-right, and right-middle circles with colours different from their neighbours as allowed by the diagram. This yields a valid colouring with 3 colours.
